## Counts

- **ACCEPTED:** 7
- **DEFERRED:** 2
- **ESTABLISHED:** 18
- **PROVISIONAL:** 5
- **REJECTED:** 4

## Decision index

| ID | Status | Title | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FAM-001 | ESTABLISHED | Standalone specialist capability boundary | Heavy domain intelligence is implemented in independently versioned capabilities rather than accumulated inside Octon Mini. |
| FAM-002 | ESTABLISHED | Harness-agnostic core | No capability core may require Octon Mini or another agent harness. |
| FAM-003 | ESTABLISHED | One authoritative engine per capability | CLI, CI, MCP, OCI, Agent Skills, harness adapters, and future HTTP must not create divergent semantic engines. |
| FAM-004 | ESTABLISHED | Evidence is not authority | Capability results never authorize repository, production, publication, deployment, database, infrastructure, or project actions. |
| FAM-005 | ESTABLISHED | Explicit permissions and effects | Capabilities declare execution, network, credential, write, and controlled-resource requirements before use. |
| FAM-006 | ESTABLISHED | No hidden installation or network | Capabilities do not silently install specialist tools or enable network access. |
| FAM-007 | ESTABLISHED | Truthful completion | Unavailable, denied, stale, unsupported, failed, timed-out, or partial work cannot appear complete or passed. |
| FAM-008 | ESTABLISHED | Agent Skills orchestrate engines | Skills teach intent routing, invocation, completion inspection, interpretation, and handoff; they do not implement domain intelligence. |
| FAM-009 | ACCEPTED | Durable result per capability | Every material capability produces an inspectable, provenance-aware durable result artifact. |
| FAM-010 | PROVISIONAL | Shared result envelope v0 | A small common envelope carries capability identity, subject, permission, completion, provenance, and payload references; domain payloads remain capability-specific. |
| FAM-011 | PROVISIONAL | Standalone capability manifest v0 | A shared discovery manifest is defined for experimentation and is not yet a stable universal standard. |
| FAM-012 | PROVISIONAL | Shared permission vocabulary | The family uses a common permission vocabulary while allowing capability-specific refinements through explicit extension. |
| FAM-013 | PROVISIONAL | Shared lifecycle convention | Discover, plan, permission review, execute/analyze, evidence, completion, durable result, inspect/compare is a reference lifecycle rather than a mandatory identical workflow. |
| FAM-014 | PROVISIONAL | Capability classes | Four descriptive classes are used for seed comparison but are not yet a stabilized taxonomy. |
| FAM-015 | ESTABLISHED | External specialist tool preference | Capabilities integrate mature specialist tools through explicit adapters when ownership would not create differentiated value. |
| FAM-016 | ACCEPTED | Out-of-process or OCI adapter boundary | Specialist adapters should normally run out of process or in OCI rather than as arbitrary in-process plugins. |
| FAM-017 | ESTABLISHED | AI is optional evidence and interpretation | AI may reason over evidence but does not become project authority, execution authority, or the sole engine. |
| FAM-018 | ESTABLISHED | Imported evidence preserves provenance | Cross-capability evidence retains source capability/version/result/completion/class/limitations and does not silently become native evidence. |
| FAM-019 | ESTABLISHED | No mandatory capability dependency cycles | Family relationships are optional evidence or aggregation unless a capability constitution explicitly establishes a hard dependency. |
| FAM-020 | ESTABLISHED | UCA is reference implementation, not universal mold | UCA proves the first pattern but its code-audit semantics are not assumed universal. |
| FAM-021 | ESTABLISHED | No universal capability framework yet | Shared runtime/framework/SDK extraction is deferred until at least three real capabilities demonstrate stable common needs. |
| FAM-022 | ACCEPTED | Verification Assurance is capability two | Verification tests whether the outer lifecycle and execution evidence model survive beyond UCA. |
| FAM-023 | ACCEPTED | Specification Conformance is capability three | Conformance tests aggregation, traceability, authority conflict, and imported evidence after UCA and Verification. |
| FAM-024 | ACCEPTED | Release Assurance is a late aggregator | Release Assurance is built after upstream result interoperability has real evidence. |
| FAM-025 | ACCEPTED | Generated platform skill adapters | Canonical skill sources generate thin platform packages with drift and behavior tests. |
| FAM-026 | ESTABLISHED | No interface authority escalation | Transport choice cannot silently grant stronger permissions or authority. |
| FAM-027 | ACCEPTED | Production-shaped products in dependency order | Each capability targets a mature v1; Minimum Complete Architecture is an integration checkpoint rather than the product ambition. |
| FAM-028 | DEFERRED | Shared family SDK | Manifest/result/completion/provenance helpers may be extracted only after demonstrated duplication. |
| FAM-029 | DEFERRED | Hosted capability service or marketplace | No central service, registry, or marketplace is required by the family architecture. |
| FAM-030 | REJECTED | Octon capability monolith | Octon Mini will not absorb specialist analysis implementations. |
| FAM-031 | REJECTED | Capability mega-engine | No single capability should absorb all testing, runtime, supply chain, browser, infrastructure, migration, and release intelligence. |
| FAM-032 | REJECTED | Skill-only capabilities | A prompt or skill cannot substitute for an independently usable engine and durable result. |
| FAM-033 | REJECTED | Automatic downstream action | Capability conclusions do not automatically create issues, mutate projects, deploy, publish, apply infrastructure, or migrate databases. |
| FAM-034 | ESTABLISHED | Canonical character identities | The ten capabilities use Verity, Titra, Ortha, Genea, Echo, Harmia, Iris, Atlas, Janus, and Sibyl as their canonical character identities without aliases or authority expansion. |
| FAM-035 | ESTABLISHED | Plectarium relationship and portfolio source ownership | Plectarium is the suite brand and part of the Octon ecosystem without becoming an Octon-prefixed product, runtime dependency, authority transfer, eleventh capability, or owner of family and capability semantics. Suite, family, capability, workspace, and harness source ownership remain separate. |
| FAM-036 | ESTABLISHED | Namespaced family identity and character repository mapping | The canonical family_id is standalone-capability-family; provisional manifest and result identities carry it alongside descriptive capability_id and capability version, and each capability repository uses its exact lowercase canonical character name. Downstream consumers pin the published family commit and packet-manifest digest instead of forking family contracts. |
